mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a single month suggests a contraction in supply-side activity, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced economic output.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it indicates strong consumer demand outpacing economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS growth exceeded GDPC1 growth in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a single month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or increasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), suggests inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns diminish.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases for 3 months and FEDFUNDS stable or increases
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL increased for three months and FEDFUNDS was stable or increased.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a single quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlooks worsen.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declined by more than 1% in a quarter.
